title: Progressive cohort spill + degenerate-model ladder for OOM-resilient continuous batching
creator: Liam Patel
description:
Problem: We see two classes of production incidents where continuous batching plus large KV working sets triggers GPU OOMs and long tail retries: (1) sudden cohort spikes with long context requests that fill KV and increase activations; (2) gradual memory pressure as background prefetch and caching for high-QPS customers accumulates. Existing mitigations (aggressive eviction, immediate model fallback, whole-request retries) either increase latency or materially hurt quality.

Goal: Implement a combined runtime-level strategy that (A) admission-controls prefetch by cohort, (B) performs progressive "spill-to-host" + NVMe staging for cold KV entries, and (C) routes requests down a degenerate-model ladder with graceful state transfer to maintain useful outputs without hard failures. This should reduce P99 OOMs by 75% for mixed-workload clusters while keeping median latency increase under 10% for affected requests.

Proposed approach:
1) Cohort-aware prefetch admission: maintain a lightweight per-cohort prefetch budget derived from historical hot-prefix retention and SLO cost budgets. Prefetch is throttled by cohort and by model-quantized memory cost (per-token KV footprint).
2) Predictive spill-to-host with async restore: when aggregate GPU memory pressure exceeds threshold, proactively spill least-recently-used KV segments to pinned host memory (and NVMe if host is saturated) using a non-blocking async restore path that attaches placeholders in the KV map so requests can continue with degraded cache hits.
3) Degenerate-model ladder: implement a sequence of compatible variants for each model (full-precision long-context -> int8-medium-context -> int4-short-context -> distilled response-only model). When a request is admitted but cannot be satisfied with full KV/state, the router attempts progressively cheaper variants while honoring prefix consistency through partial KV replay where possible.
4) SLO-aware retry/backoff and request shaping: instead of immediate full retry, use fast-path heuristics to return a partial streaming response with an indication of degraded context, plus an optional background retry to attempt higher-fidelity completion (useful for async clients).

Trade-offs considered: aggressive spill may increase tail latency for specific requests due to NVMe hops; degenerate-model ladder may produce shorter or lower-quality answers for some customers. To mitigate customer impact we will: (a) expose per-customer preference flags (prefer-quality / prefer-latency), (b) limit ladder depth for enterprise SLAs, (c) log and tag any degraded-response for downstream evals.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for async spill/restore correctness and KV placeholder semantics.
- Performance test: synthetic mixed workload (30% long-context heavy cohort, 70% short queries) shows >=75% reduction in P99 OOM incidents on staging cluster and <=10% median latency regression for affected requests.
- Gradual canary rollout with observability flags and automatic rollback on increased error or quality regression signals.
